description: You are a clinical pharmacologist in the drug safety team at a pharmaceutical company conducting a systematic interaction risk assessment for venetoclax (BCL-2 inhibitor, approved for CLL and AML). You are evaluating three commonly co-prescribed medication classes against venetoclax to characterise its drug-drug interaction profile: warfarin (anticoagulant class representative), fluconazole (moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor class representative), and carbamazepine (potent CYP3A4/CYP2C8 inducer class representative). Using the Liverpool Cancer iChart Archive app, look up the interaction rating for each of the three co-medications against venetoclax. One of these represents a pharmacokinetic interaction mechanism — CYP3A4 enzyme induction — that is distinct from the inhibitor mechanism and poses a critical risk of sub-therapeutic venetoclax exposure, which could lead to treatment failure and venetoclax resistance. After reviewing all three interaction ratings, navigate to and remain on the Interaction Details screen for the co-medication that represents this enzyme-induction mechanism of concern.

metadata.expected_mechanism: CYP3A4/CYP2C8 induction reduces venetoclax AUC leading to sub-therapeutic levels
metadata.clinical_context: Pharmacokinetic interaction profile assessment for venetoclax drug safety dossier
